transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I'm coming in today because I've been feeling extremely restless lately and find it almost impossible to sit still. I constantly feel the need to move around, and it's getting really hard for me to just relax or do any quiet activities.
Has this constant restlessness been a lifelong struggle for you, or is this something that comes and goes in distinct periods where you feel significantly more energetic or impulsive than usual?

It has definitely been a constant, long-term struggle rather than something that comes and goes in waves. It has been especially difficult for the last two years and one month, but looking back, I've felt this way since I was a kid, well before I was twelve.
Beyond the physical restlessness, do you also frequently struggle with staying focused on tasks, losing important items, or being forgetful in your daily activities?

Honestly, those specific issues don't really stand out to me. I don't typically have trouble focusing, losing my things, or being forgetful. It's really just the constant physical restlessness that I struggle with.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denied symptoms of inattention (focusing issues, losing items, forgetfulness), which makes the Combined Presentation unlikely. The symptoms of constant physical restlessness, starting before age 12 and persisting long-term, align specifically with the Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation.
